transcript.text: “Won’t come on” can mean either completely dead, or powered but refusing to start. The quickest split is whether any lights/display appear. 1. Check the plug is fully in and the dishwasher’s switched spur/socket is on. If safe to do so, try another appliance in that socket. If the consumer unit has tripped, do not keep resetting it. A dead socket points to the supply rather than the dishwasher. 2. If it has lights, open the door and check no rack, plate or utensil is preventing it closing. Shut it firmly until it clicks, select a programme and press Start. If it has power but will not begin, the door latch/interlock is a common cause. 3. Look for a padlock/key symbol or a delay countdown; a control lock or delay start can stop the buttons or make it appear not to start. When you press the on/off button, are there any lights or display at all? If not, does the socket or switched spur supply power to another appliance?
no lights or display at all, completely dead. other sockets and lights in the kitchen work fine. the spur switch is on and its neon is lit

A lit neon on the spur shows the spur has a supply, but it does not prove power is reaching the dishwasher itself. The main possibilities are a failed fused-spur/output supply or fuse, versus a fault in the dishwasher’s mains input/control board. 1. If the dishwasher plug and socket are safely accessible, switch the dishwasher off, unplug it, then try a known-working small appliance in that exact socket. Do not pull the dishwasher out or remove any covers just to reach it. • If the test appliance does not work, this is an electrical supply/fused-spur issue: use an electrician. • If it does work, the dishwasher has an internal power fault, most commonly its mains input wiring/filter or control board, and an appliance engineer should diagnose it. If it is hard-wired or the socket is inaccessible, don’t open the spur or appliance yourself; an engineer can confirm the supply and internal fault safely.
it's an integrated one, so I can't pull it out to get to the plug. I don't have a spare fuse or a meter either. What do I do then?

With an integrated dishwasher and no accessible plug, there is no further safe owner check that will separate this. Do not remove the dishwasher or open the fused spur yourself. A lit neon only shows that the spur has an incoming supply; it does not prove its fuse, cable or outlet is supplying the dishwasher. The two live possibilities are a fault at the fused spur/output supply, or an internal dishwasher power fault such as its mains input wiring/filter or control board. Book an appliance engineer if you want the dishwasher diagnosed; they can safely prove the supply at the appliance and then test the internal power side. If the spur itself is suspected or needs work, that part should be dealt with by an electrician.

candidates: No mains supply or switched spur/socket issue (high)
Door not latching or door interlock fault (medium)
Control lock, delay setting or control fault (medium)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
